summary:
SPHEREx TimeLens is an open-source scientific exploration backend for accessing and inspecting real SPHEREx infrared observations by celestial coordinates and wavelength.

Users can provide ICRS right ascension and declination to search NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) SIA2 for SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 spectral-image products or discover tiles from the DR1 All-Sky Cube.

The system is designed to retrieve genuine FITS products, validate their structure, extract selected spectral channels from the 102-channel cube, mask pixels without observational coverage using NHITS, and read wavelength information from SPECTRAL_CHANNELS. It produces display-only PNG previews with archive provenance and coverage information.

Our goal is to make specialist infrared astronomical data easier to explore while maintaining scientific transparency and reproducibility. The current deliverable is a tested API backend. A complete graphical explorer, temporal image comparison, and moving-object classification remain future development.
details:
SPHEREx TimeLens is a Python-based astronomical data exploration system developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

1. Coordinate-Based Archive Discovery

The backend accepts celestial coordinates using Right Ascension and Declination in the ICRS coordinate system. It validates the input and queries NASA/IPAC IRSA through its Simple Image Access Version 2 interface.

It supports discovery of SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 spectral-image collections and the separate DR1 All-Sky Cube collection.

2. SPHEREx FITS Cube Exploration

The system retrieves supported DR1 All-Sky Cube products from the official IRSA HTTPS archive.

It inspects the multi-extension FITS structure and extracts individual spectral channels from the IMAGE extension.

It also reads the SPECTRAL_CHANNELS metadata and uses NHITS to identify pixels with valid observational coverage. FLAGS provides additional diagnostic information, and channels marked blank through the BLANKCH header are rejected.

3. Scientific Image Preview

The backend generates grayscale PNG previews using percentile-based intensity normalization.

Each preview includes information about its source archive, spectral channel, wavelength when available, coverage fraction, and units.

These images are visualization products, not calibrated photometry measurements.

4. Engineering and Reliability

The implementation includes coordinate validation, restricted archive download URLs, bounded FITS downloads, API error handling, and automated tests.

Generated FITS fixtures and mocked archive responses are used for software testing, and are not represented as real astronomical observations.

GitHub Actions automatically runs the backend test suite.

5. Technology and Tools

  • Python 3.11
  • FastAPI and Uvicorn
  • Astroquery and Astropy
  • NumPy
  • Requests
  • Pillow
  • Pytest and HTTPX
  • GitHub Actions
  • Claude , ChatGPT
  • Google Gemini

6. Innovation and Intended Impact

TimeLens connects astronomical coordinate searches to actual SPHEREx spectral-image and cube products. Its emphasis on wavelength metadata, observation coverage, and archive provenance makes it possible to inspect the data without treating every unusual image feature as a scientific discovery.

The broader objective is to develop this foundation into a chronological infrared sky exploration platform supporting spatial WCS visualization, compatible multi-epoch comparisons, and evidence-based investigation of changing celestial sources.

Current Development Limitations

The public development branch currently provides archive discovery, cube channel extraction, coverage-aware previews, and automated backend tests.

Live end-to-end archive retrieval has not yet been independently verified. A deployed graphical frontend, spatial WCS sky rendering, temporal blink comparison, Gaia cross-matching, and moving-object detection are not yet implemented.
